S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by at least six months of disturbance, including at least one month of active-phase symptoms such as delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking or behavior, and/or prominent negative symptoms like diminished emotional expression or avolition. It typically emerges in late adolescence or early adulthood and follows a variable course, with many patients experiencing relapsing episodes superimposed on persistent functional impairment. Distinguishing features include the presence of clear psychotic symptoms and social/occupational decline not better explained by mood disorders with psychotic features, substance use, or medical conditions. Cognitive deficits, impaired insight, and difficulties in role functioning are common and often drive help‑seeking when they disrupt work, relationships, or independent living.

patient.stressor: About a year before presentation, Nancy was promoted informally into a de facto lead role in her transportation operations office, taking on more complex routing projects and mentoring several new hires while still covering her regular workload. Over the following months, her normally meticulous planning began to slip at work, with increasing difficulty completing route maps on time and a growing pattern of tense interactions with drivers and customers, which she attributed at first to "burnout" and long hours. Her supervisors noted repeated errors and uncharacteristic confusion during dispatch crises, and she started missing softball games, choir rehearsals, and even a few church commitments as she struggled to keep up, leading to conflict with colleagues and embarrassment in her close‑knit community. When a serious routing mistake led to a near‑miss safety incident and formal write‑up, her husband and manager jointly urged her to see a psychiatrist because she was insisting that others were sabotaging her work and refusing to accept coaching, making it clear that something beyond ordinary job stress was impairing her functioning.
patient.chief_complaint: “People at work are plotting against me and changing my routes on purpose, and no one believes me when I tell them it’s happening.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: At work I can feel the others coordinating behind my back—like when a route I drew up gets mysteriously changed in the system or a driver shows up with a different printout, I know someone is sneaking in after me to alter things just to make me look incompetent, even though my boss keeps saying it’s just ‘computer glitches.’

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: Sometimes in the middle of a busy shift I just freeze at my desk, staring at the screen or holding the phone without answering it, or I start pacing up and down the hallway and muttering through the routes under my breath while everyone else is trying to work, and I can’t seem to make myself act ‘normal’ even when I know people are watching me weirdly.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: Over these past months I’ve stopped caring about pretty much everything—my choir, softball, even going to church or talking with friends—and most days after work I just lie on the couch in my uniform, not showering or cooking, answering my husband with one‑word replies because it feels like too much effort to feel anything or do anything at all.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because of all this, I’m on a final warning at work for mistakes and ‘attitude,’ I’ve basically dropped out of my choir and softball team, and at home my husband is frustrated that I barely help with chores or engage in our life together anymore.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, all of this—the slipping at work, pulling away from people, and feeling more and more off—has been building for most of the past year since I was pushed into that lead role.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: The clear sense that coworkers are plotting and secretly changing my routes has really only taken over in the last couple of months, going from a nagging suspicion to something I can’t shake at all.
